To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

we have designed and analyzed an algorithm that achieves minimax rates in the global optimization of Lipschitiz functions and that we have introduced an adaptive version of the algorithm that achieves the same rates without any prior knowledge of the Lipschitz parameter.

we provide the first general framework for global optimization of Lipschiz functions; we design and analyze two algorithms that are consistent and efficient in the minimax sense; we prove fast rates of convergence for the first algorithm under a Hölder like condition and for the adaptive algorithm under the additional assumption that the function is smooth; we provide a numerical assessment to show the potential of our approach with respect to state of the art algorithms over typical benchmark problems
we propose a new method for global optimization of Lipschiz functions which has a fast convergence rate and is adaptive to the unknown Lipschitz constant.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the design and the analysis of efficient strategies for global optimization of Lipschitiz functions.
the design of efficient algorithms to optimize a Lipschitz function over a compact domain.
global optimization of an unknown Lipschitz function.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the Lipschitz condition is a very strong assumption and it is very unlikely that the minimax rate of convergence can be achieved in practice.
Lipschitz global optimization is possible and that the LIPO algorithm is a promising candidate for the task.
the proposed algorithms are able to efficiently solve a large class of problems for which no efficient algorithms are available.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the Lipschitz assumption is a powerful assumption which allows for a very general theory and for efficient algorithms.
we have provided a first step towards the design of a generic sequential algorithm for global optimization of Lipschiz functions.

, for the first time, a sequential algorithm for global Lipschitz optimization has been shown to be minimax rate optimal in the sense that its expected convergence rate is within a logarithmic factor of the minimax rate.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the Lipschitz condition can be a useful assumption to derive theoretical properties for global optimization and that it can be exploited by a simple and efficient strategy.
, when the Lipschitz assumption is satisfied, the global optimization problem can be tackled in an efficient manner by sequential algorithms.
Lipschitz continuity of the objective function is not a restrictive assumption in the context of global optimization, and that the minimax rate is attained by the proposed LIPO algorithm.
